messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: encoder-service rollout v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 (canary 10%)

maya: seeing increased 502s on the canary endpoints, starting alerts.

raj: checking k8s — a bunch of encoder pods in CrashLoopBackOff on node-gpu-12. grabbing logs now.

maya: copying alert graphs — p95 latency on /generate jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s, error rate ~12% for the canary. Customer-facing.

raj: logs show OOMKilled then crashloop: "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space" inside encoder container. image v2.5.0 seems to use more memory for kv-cache.

li: HPA config for encoder-target is weird — minReplicas: 0 in the canary namespace due to a templating bug. that means autoscaler didn't spin up extra pods during thundering bursts.

oncall-sre: paging in. assigning incident lead: maya.

maya: quick mitigation options: 1) kill canary traffic (feature flag) 2) scale encoder replicas manually 3) rollback to v2.4.1. Suggest kill flag + scale while we assess.

sam-cs: customers reporting 502s from EU region, some important accounts impacted. CS is notifying top 10 customers.

li: I can flip the canary flag in LaunchDarkly now — toggling traffic back to stable. executing: `curl -X POST https://ff.redwood-internal/api/toggles/encoder_canary -d '{"enabled": false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'`

ops-bot: Feature flag toggle executed by li at 2026-03-17T14:25:12Z — canary traffic set to 0%.

raj: scaling encoder deployment in canary namespace: `kubectl scale deploy encoder --replicas=4 -n canary` — starting pods.

maya: also doing `kubectl get pods -n canary -o wide` to ensure pods land on different nodes. hitting GPU node taints? will check affinities.

raj: found node-gpu-12 had stale GPU driver after last maintenance causing memory leak under certain workload patterns. tainted it: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12` and evicted failing pods.

maya: error rate dropped to 1.2% after killing canary traffic and scaling. latency trending back down.

li: still seeing a subset of v2.5.0 pods restart on non-gpu nodes and crash due to missing nvlib dependencies — missing daemonset change in the chart. that's on me.

maya: for immediate safety let's roll back the canary deployment to v2.4.1 to remove the new memory pattern from any remaining traffic path. executing: `kubectl -n canary rollout undo deployment/encoder --to-revision=3`

ops-bot: Rollout undo initiated by maya at 2026-03-17T14:34:02Z.

raj: rollback finished, pods stable on v2.4.1, no CrashLoopBackOff observed.

maya: status update: mitigation = feature flag kill + scale + rollback. customer error rates returned to baseline within ~8 minutes of flag flip. alerting quieting.

sam-cs: customers informed. major accounts acknowledged; one had a brief SLA blip, CS will track for credits if needed.

li: root cause summary so far: 1) v2.5.0 increased memory usage (kv-cache) 2) chart templating bug set HPA minReplicas=0 in canary -> underprovision during burst 3) missing GPU runtime dependency caused cross-node failures 4) one node had driver regression that worsened OOM.

maya: next actions: - fix chart templating to enforce minReplicas>=2 for encoder - add preflight check in CI to detect increased RSS/heap in integration runs - pin v2.5.0 to internal canary until deps validated - node maintenance + driver rollback scheduled

raj: I'll open a PR for chart change and add a k8s admission test to prevent minReplicas=0.

li: I'll add the missing daemonset change and a compatibility test for nvlib in our CI. also will run a memory-profiling job for v2.5.0.

maya: postmortem owner = maya. target postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow. ops severity = Sev2 (customer impact, short duration).

ops-bot: Incident incident-1768999999 created, severity=2, lead=maya, timeline recorded.

sam-cs: thanks team — CS will follow up with affected customers and send the incident summary once postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:

maya: handing off to oncall-sre for overnight watch. ping me if cpu/mem alerts re-spike.

oncall-sre: acknowledged, taking over monitoring.

maya: closing thread as mitigation complete; will keep channel updated for postmortem link.
